exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Joining a Charity Run
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Hi Tom, are you free next Sunday? I'm joining a charity run for the children's hospital.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: A charity run? That sounds great. How far do you have to run?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Just five kilometres. You don't have to be fast; you only have to finish.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: And how does the run raise money?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Friends and family promise to donate some money for every runner who finishes.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That's a clever idea. Can I still sign up?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Of course. You just fill in a form online and pay a small fee.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Brilliant. Let's train together this week so we're both ready.

exercises.translation_cn: Mia 邀请 Tom 下周日参加为儿童医院举办的慈善跑;只需跑五公里、跑完即可,不必跑得快;亲友为每位完赛者捐款;Tom 想报名,只需网上填表并交一点费用;两人决定本周一起训练。

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Charity Shops
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: On many British high streets, you will find charity shops.
These shops sell second-hand clothes, books and toys that people no longer want.
Kind volunteers, not paid workers, run most of them.
The money from each sale goes to a good cause, such as fighting cancer or helping the homeless.
Shopping there is good for everyone, so next time you pass a charity shop, why not step inside?
exercises.translation_cn: 在英国许多商业街上你会看到慈善商店;这些店出售人们不再需要的二手衣物、书籍和玩具;大多由志愿者而非雇员经营;每笔收入都用于慈善事业,如抗癌或帮助无家可归者;在那里购物对大家都有好处,下次路过不妨进去看看。

questions.stem: What do charity shops mainly sell?

options: Fighting cancer or helping the homeless.

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest doing?
options: Stepping inside a charity shop next time.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 A Phone Enquiry
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: Good morning, Greenfield Volunteer Centre. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Hello. I'd like to become a volunteer. Could you tell me what work you have?

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: Certainly. We need people to help teach children with disabilities at a riding centre.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: That sounds perfect. I love horses and I enjoy being with children.

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: Wonderful. We'd like you to help out three times a week, if possible.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: That's fine. What do I need to do to start?

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: Just fill in a registration form. We'll then send you a letter of confirmation.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Thank you. Is there anything else I should know?

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: We'll also ask about any experience you have, but don't worry, training is provided.

exercises.translation_cn: Sarah 打电话到志愿者中心,想做志愿者并询问有什么工作;中心需要人在马术中心帮忙教残障儿童;Sarah 喜欢马也喜欢和孩子相处;中心希望她每周帮三次;开始前需填登记表,中心会寄确认信;还会询问经验,但提供培训。

questions.stem: Why is Sarah calling the centre?

options: Teaching children with disabilities at a riding centre.

questions.stem: How often does the centre want Sarah to help?

options: Pay a large sum of money.

options: They will ask about it, but training is provided.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Everyone Can Make a Difference
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: You might think that only rich or famous people can help the world, but that is not true.
Making a difference does not always need money.
You can give your time, your skills, or simply your kindness.
Visit a lonely neighbour, plant a tree, or help a classmate who is behind.
Small actions, repeated by many people, can change a whole community.
So the right question is not 'Why should I help?' but 'How can I help today?'
exercises.translation_cn: 你也许以为只有富人或名人才能帮助世界,其实不然;有所作为并不总需要金钱;你可以付出时间、技能,或仅仅一份善意;探望孤独的邻居、种一棵树,或帮助落后的同学;许多人的微小行动能改变整个社区;关键问题不是'我为什么要帮',而是'我今天能怎么帮'。

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 A Book Donation
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Anna, our class is collecting books for a village school. Would you like to help?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'd love to. What kind of books do they need?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Mostly storybooks and simple science books for younger children.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I have a whole box of old picture books at home, and they're in good condition.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: That's wonderful. Could you bring them to school on Friday?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sure. Should we clean them first?

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Yes, please. We want every book to look nice for the children.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No problem. It feels great to give my old books a new home.

exercises.translation_cn: Leo 说班里在为一所乡村学校收集图书,问 Anna 是否帮忙;学校主要需要故事书和给低龄孩子的简单科普书;Anna 家有一整箱品相不错的旧绘本;Leo 请她周五带到学校;还要先把书擦干净;Anna 很乐意,觉得让旧书有个新归宿很好。

options: A box of old picture books.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Why People Volunteer
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Have you ever wondered why so many people give their free time to help others for no pay?
When you ask volunteers, their answers are often surprising.
Some say that helping others makes them feel useful and happy.
Others enjoy learning new skills or making new friends.
A few simply want to thank the world for the good luck they have had.
Whatever the reason, one thing is clear: when you help someone else, you often help yourself as well.
exercises.translation_cn: 你是否想过,为什么这么多人愿意无偿付出空闲时间去帮助别人?问问志愿者,他们的回答常常出人意料:有人说助人让自己感到有用又快乐;有人喜欢学习新技能、结交新朋友;也有人只是想回报自己拥有的好运;无论原因如何,有一点很清楚:当你帮助别人时,你往往也帮助了自己。
